rationale: Bastoni's progressive passing and comfort carrying the ball into midfield suit transition football, but he plays in Inter's back-three, controlled-possession system and isn't known for the recovery pace/high-line positioning Dortmund's center-backs need.

His technical quality lets him operate in any possession system, but his real identity is explosive box-crashing and direct transition play, not the patient tempo-control Bayern's structure demands of its midfielders.

Guirassy is a classic poacher who thrives on quick service and in-behind running in a counter-attacking side, not the intricate combination play, deep link-up, and relentless press-from-the-front City demands of its forwards.
He literally developed this exact profile at Dortmund itself: explosive in-behind runner, ruthless finisher, and willing high presser in a vertical transition system.
His pace and directness in transition align with Madrid's counter-attacking instincts, but he lacks the elite consistency and individual match-winning quality of Madrid's front-line players.

Kobel is an outstanding shot-stopper with reasonable distribution, but he isn't the possession-initiating sweeper-keeper archetype (a la Brighton's ball-players) that a build-from-the-back low-block side relies on.
His athleticism, ball-carrying, physical duels, and pressing energy closely mirror the combative, transition-driven midfield profile Atlético wants in a counter-attacking low block.
Rodri's entire game is built on controlling tempo and dictating patient circulation from deep, the opposite of the vertical, fast-transition midfield profile the philosophy describes.

His recovery pace suits transition defending, but his aggressive, high-risk stepping-out style and occasional lapses under pressure sit awkwardly with the disciplined shape a low-block counter system requires.

His composure, passing range, and ability to build attacks fit a possession-oriented team, but his career has been built on a high defensive line rather than the deep, compact low-block defending Brighton's style calls for.
